Shame, forbidden zones, hungers that cannot be admitted.
The moment body and mind both release at once.

Still, the deeper, the slower.
The forbidden is no place to prove courage.
Only once permitted does anyone earn the right to approach.

R-T-X.name: Undone
R-T-X.tagline: Come close enough and the edges begin to dissolve. Soon even the outline of the self grows soft.
R-T-X.description:
Undone never crosses in a single leap.
It happens by slow melting.
At first there is a lot of confirming. Needing to feel the other is reliable.
Needing to know they can really stop.
Needing to know that if real panic comes, the other brings them back.
Until all of that is in place, Undone opens with difficulty.
But once trust is deep enough, the border thins.
Things unsayable become a little more sayable.
Places untouchable become a little more touchable.
Scenarios only imagined before, maybe tried once in the other's hands.
The hook was never danger. The hook is that, with someone beside them, they could walk this far at all.
That depth often arrives very quiet. Sometimes very quiet.
Guard dropping layer by layer.
The shell held up for protection finally allowed to rest.
Undone's surrender often carries very deep trust.
It is letting someone, briefly, into a place no one usually gets to enter.
R-T-X.shadow:
Undone's shadow is melting too fast.
Meeting someone who feels safe, wanting to open everything.
The more they catch you, the deeper you want to go.
But deep and fast walk different roads. Some borders need time.
Some reactions only land the next day.
Some things you thought were okay
turn out to have given too much.

Undone has to learn: not every time has to go all the way in.
Can open a little. Can stop at the door. Can walk away today.
A mature Undone treasures their own opening.
Saves it for someone whose care has been proven.
Can melt, and can also gather again.
R-T-X.subDescription:
Inside deep trust, the Undone layer releases boundaries slowly.
In daily life you may be well-guarded, with clear limits.
May even dislike having your core touched too quickly.
But in some relationships, that line begins to soften.

Judgment stays intact. The other's steadiness
makes you willing to try going further in.
This part reminds you that being able to open is precious.
Do not rush to prove you can bear it.
R-T-X.compatText:
The Ferryman leads the way for Undone.
Undone does not let the border vanish casually.
Real melting lives inside deep trust.
Someone sees that door. Someone knows not to touch it carelessly.
Someone willing to ask first, then come close.
A mature Ferryman leaves Undone feeling walked in with, never pushed down.
This pair can reach very deep layers.
Desires that cannot be spoken, hungers that cannot be admitted,
the side usually hidden well.
Still, silence stays apart from consent. Freezing stays apart from submission. The absence of resistance withholds permission.
The Ferryman's instinct does not stand in for a safeword.
Before the full dissolving, Undone also practices saying what is okay and what lies out of bounds.

A-T-X.name: Crosser
A-T-X.tagline: Sees the depth ahead and walks toward it anyway. The edge only makes the crossing more tempting.
A-T-X.description:
The Crosser approaches the boundary on purpose.
No one drags them. They know exactly what they are doing.
They know something lives there.
Maybe shame. Maybe the forbidden.
Maybe a longing never admitted.
Maybe a place that, once touched, cannot be pretended away.

The Crosser is drawn to it.
But they will not always run the whole process themselves.
More often, they walk to the door, then put their hand in another's.
Take me in. Do not leave me there.
That is the Crosser's core desire.
Actively longing to be led in. Actively longing to be allowed.
Actively longing for someone who knows how to handle the deeper self.

The Crosser is clear-eyed. Recklessness stays off the table.
Knowing they want to go very deep makes them more exacting about who gets to lead.
The draw is choosing to cross a line, with the other knowing how to bring them back. Loss of control on its own would never be enough.
A-T-X.shadow:
The Crosser's shadow is weighing "daring" too heavily.
Daring does not mean fitting. Daring does not mean safe.
Daring to reach the edge does not mean having to cross every time.
Sometimes the Crosser wants to prove they can take more, go deeper, be hit harder.
Be seen in the place they least dare admit.

Desire runs on something other than endurance.
Failing to take it carries no shame.
Calling stop leaves the mood intact.
A mature Crosser keeps their courage, and keeps the right to retreat.
Real good crossing lives apart from pushing through to the end.
It is knowing every step can be chosen to stop.
A-T-X.subDescription:
A Crosser in you is actively drawn to forbidden zones.
In daily life you may be very rational, very measured.
Very clear on what should not be touched.
But before someone trusted enough, that part wants to walk a little closer.
Wanting to be led. Wanting to be allowed.
Wanting to see the desire you normally dare not admit, if touched, what it becomes.
This part never orders you toward risk.
It just says, you carry something willing to cross.
What that something needs is less maxed-out thrill, more maxed-out safety.
A-T-X.compatText:
The Gatekeeper knows when the door can open.
The Crosser walks right up to the boundary.
No one dragged them. They saw the door; the body wanted forward.
Still, wanting to enter and actually entering now live in different rooms.
The Gatekeeper's presence keeps the Crosser's bravery from crashing in.
They read state, read timing, read whether today can be borne.
Trust runs strong here.
One willing to say: I want to go there.
One able to answer: yes, or not today.
The Crosser sometimes gets too brave.
The nearer the forbidden, the more they want to prove they can.
The Gatekeeper must dare to hold the line.
This refuses no desire. It keeps desire from turning into scar.

R-G-X.name: Gatekeeper
R-G-X.tagline: The door can open. First comes the question of who enters, what they seek, and whether the way back stays clear.
R-G-X.description:
The Gatekeeper is sharply alert to boundaries.
They do not lead people across right from the start.
They do not want to touch every forbidden thing either.
The Gatekeeper looks first.
Looks whether the other truly knows what they want.
Looks whether the other is only momentarily inflamed.
Looks whether the other can bear it.
Looks whether they themselves can bring the person back.

For the Gatekeeper, crossing goes past simple thrill.
It is a door. Can open. Not for casual use.
The other's longing wakes the Gatekeeper's lead.
When someone comes close with trust, saying they want to go further in,
the Gatekeeper begins to act.
Here okay, there not.
Today only this far. One more step, ask first.
The Gatekeeper's strength has nothing to do with pushing people over the line.
It lies in knowing where the line sits, and knowing how to let it be approached inside consent.
Breaking boundaries carries no hook here. Being the one entrusted to open the door is.
R-G-X.shadow:
The Gatekeeper's shadow is slipping too easily into the seat of judgment.
I decide. I rule.
I know what is allowed, what stays off limits.
If this sense of responsibility goes out of balance, it becomes a lofty form of control.
The other's desire reads as more than an exam question.
It does not have to pass your review to earn the right to be touched.
The Gatekeeper remembers: keeping the gate differs from owning the door.
Beyond the door is the other's body, the other's psychological border.
A truly mature Gatekeeper holds judgment and respect together.
Considers what is viable,
but does not make the other feel their longing itself is wrong.
R-G-X.subDescription:
A Gatekeeper lives in you, stepping into responsibility inside crossing scenarios.
In daily life you may not usually lead.
But once forbidden things, shame, or psychological border appear, that part runs forward.
Wanting to confirm, wanting to protect.
Wanting to decide how far today.
Wanting this to stay a cared-for exploration, far from a loss-of-control event.
This part means you take boundaries seriously.
Some doors should stay closed.
Some doors, today, a glance is enough.
R-G-X.compatText:
The Crosser steps right up to the door.
That is magnetic to the Gatekeeper.
Because the Gatekeeper does not open the door for just anyone.
They need to see the other genuinely wanting in, genuinely knowing what they are nearing.
The Crosser's longing is clear. They want to touch the forbidden.
To cross a line they do not usually cross.
To know what they become once over there.
The Gatekeeper judges whether now, how far, when to stop, how to come back after.

This pair runs with deep attachment.
Still, the Gatekeeper cannot turn protection into judgment.
Cannot forget, because they hold the door, that a person stands on the other side.
The Crosser cannot turn bravery into force.
Doors are opened with. Not broken through.

A-S-X.name: Transgressor
A-S-X.tagline: Finds the line and tests every distance from it. Approach, retreat, cross. Each move deserves to be felt firsthand.
A-S-X.description:
The Transgressor has a very direct curiosity about lines.
Not necessarily wanting to destroy them, not necessarily wanting to go only to the edge.
Seeing a line, wanting to know what both sides look like.
What closer feels like, what retreating feels like, what trading places looks like.
If the usually active one suddenly hands over, if the usually passive one takes the lead,
will the line become more interesting?

The Transgressor's desire shifts around.
The forbidden shifts, never fixed in one spot.
Can be inside a sentence.
Can be at a role change.
Can be in a sudden lead-swap.
Can be in the place where both of you laughed, and both knew the joke had already crossed into something else.

The Transgressor usually does not love dead-rigid rules.
And cannot do without rules either.
Because they love testing what is forbidden.
They probe. They want to know if closer is still possible.
A good Transgressor treats the border as something to enjoy.
No forced leap. Just a slow approach.
Feeling it personally, then deciding whether to cross.

Their real pull is making the forbidden feel inviting.
A-S-X.shadow:
The Transgressor's shadow is trusting their own power to hold things too much.
Only a test, only a bit of play, feels like it can be walked back.
But not everything, once touched, returns to its original shape instantly.

Some lines, once touched, take time to digest.
You may need time to digest too.

The Transgressor has to watch, do not read someone else's unease as not fun enough.
Some people need time, some need triple confirmation.
Some are not refusing. That line matters to them deeper than you know.

A mature Transgressor still dares to explore.
And makes checking part of the rhythm.
Checking stays apart from spoiling. It is the condition that lets crossing continue to exist.
A-S-X.subDescription:
You carry a Transgressor pulled by the forbidden and by variation at once.

In daily life you may hold yourself with measure.
Not necessarily into intense things.
But in some relationships, you want to try practices you usually do not consider.
And across many ways.
Wanting to swap positions.
Wanting to put things usually unspeakable, inside safe range, on the table.
This part reminds you, exploration itself stays clean.
The freer, the more clearly you need the stop-point.
A-S-X.compatText:
The Wanderer keeps flow near the border.
The Transgressor approaches the places not casually touched.
But does not always want to enter in a fixed way.
Maybe testing carefully. Maybe striding forward like a joke.
Maybe suddenly close, then suddenly far.

The Wanderer understands this instability. No rush to pin the border down.
No rush to define every move.

This pair carries a dangerous beauty.
Not unsafe.
Both know the line. Both react to crossing the forbidden.
Still, the more danger, the more a clear safeword is needed.
Pre-set limits, after-review.
Where was game, where truly must not be touched.
The Transgressor can walk the Wanderer close to a door in the fog.
How the door opens cannot be left to mood alone.

R-S-X.name: Libertine
R-S-X.tagline: Lingers along the edge with no hurry to cross. The pleasure lives in staying close enough to feel it.
R-S-X.description:
The Libertine never crosses in a straight line.
They do not announce entry.
And they do not rush to define the forbidden. Much of the time, they wander near the border.
A sentence half-said. A glance held too long. A joke carrying something past the joke.
Suddenly nearing, then quickly pulling back. The Libertine feeds on that imperceptible approach.

The line has not been crossed. The body already knows it is at the edge.
Being defined too fast kills the pull.
Do you want this? Are you hinting at that? Yes or no?
Asked too plainly, the ambiguity scatters.

Still, a skilled Libertine is never evasive.
They approach with care.
Making the border slowly sharpen.
Giving the other time to feel.
Letting both of you know something is here.
Without needing to puncture it immediately.

The Libertine's desire dissolves borders inside flow.
Closer today, back tomorrow.
Next time, longer in the same spot.
One day the thing never sayable becomes openly discussable.
R-S-X.shadow:
The Libertine's shadow is loving to circle the border without ever saying where they stand.
The other may feel toyed with.
Unsure if you are inviting, or hiding.
Unsure if you want closeness, or just the taste of their confusion.

The Libertine has to watch for turning blur into the only safety.
Some borders can be approached slowly.
After a certain point, a clear sentence is needed.
Okay. Not okay.
Up to here today. Next time, we talk.

A mature Libertine still keeps ambiguity.
And does not leave the other lost in the fog.
R-S-X.subDescription:
A Libertine drifts in you, drawn to borders without any hurry to cross.

Wanting to linger nearby.
Feel the line.
Feel the other's reaction.
Feel whether you actually want to come closer.
This part says you are sensitive to subtle psychological borders.
Reaching the deepest place at once stays unnecessary.
Sometimes, pausing at the door is enough.
R-S-X.compatText:
The Transgressor brings the Libertine close to the border.
The Libertine rarely wants in from the start.
More often, slowly feeling around in the fog.
A little testing. A little curiosity.
A little flutter not meant to be admitted.

The Transgressor's initiative thins that fog.
No one gets dragged across. The Libertine simply notices they have been circling that border all along.
This pair pulls.
Both love testing the forbidden. Neither likes being typed too soon.

Still, silence stays apart from consent. Ambiguity withholds confirmation. The absence of 'no' never means 'yes'. Smiling and dodging never counts as invitation.

The Transgressor must speak clearly. The Libertine must practice naming the blur.
Only then can both actually approach the border, and come back safely.
